name: Silas Weir
whyHere: You finished something. Completely. It nearly got you exiled, and you are still not sure they were wrong.

inventory.name: Traveler's Pack
inventory.description: A worn canvas pack with good straps — bedroll, flint, mess kit, fifty small comforts of the road.

inventory.name: Waterskin
inventory.description: Boiled and refilled at the last clean spring. Worth more every week the river runs gray.

inventory.name: Belt Knife
inventory.description: A plain working blade — more tool than weapon, but it has been both.

inventory.name: Hemp Rope (30 ft)
inventory.description: Tarred hemp, knotted every arm's length. The difference between a fall and a climb.

inventory.name: Preserved Trail Parcel
inventory.description: Aldric's smokehouse goods — dried river perch and salted pork, cloth-wrapped and knotted. Holds a week on the road. Two parcels.

inventory.name: Assembled Mid-Weight Spear
inventory.description: A seasoned ash shaft six feet long with the mid-weight iron tip road-lashed at the socket throat — wide-cut blade, cross-guard shoulder, oiled leather binding. Four threads seated: ironsense as anchor, Huginn's Ashwarden ending-sense through the fuller, a shadow-harm focus at the quillon, and an order-sense capacitor closed on Pell's reading idiom. The maker's mark is Pell's. Silas's…
inventory.provenance: Rune-bound at the Fell Pell on World-day 18 evening, with Huginn as witness at the stone ring.

inventory.name: Valve Failure Timeline (note)
inventory.description: A small torn page in Mara's hand — four sleeve blank sales, four failure dates, two customer names. World-day minus-eighteen: Fen's intake. World-day minus-nine: east furlong farmer.

inventory.name: Contact Names Scrap (Sorel, Leth)
inventory.description: A chalk-written scrap from Mara — two names from the old pass circuit with Edge District ties. Sorel: spice-broker, wintered in the Edge District two years. Leth: archivist type, likely still there.

inventory.name: Hard Tallow Block
inventory.description: Rendered and pressed flat — good for leather, boots, rope-ends, and a dozen trail needs.

inventory.name: Oilcloth Fold
inventory.description: Heavy enough to shed a night of rain, light enough to pack small.

inventory.name: Pine-Tar Salve Tin
inventory.description: Dara's recipe — for cracked skin, rope-burn, and anything the cold gets into.

inventory.name: River Whetstone (Pell's)
inventory.description: A smooth river-flat whetstone — Pell's own. It belongs to the bench beside the sword now.

inventory.name: Fendt's Testimony (folded page)
inventory.description: A single page in Fendt's hand — dates, seventh-band designations, the nine-day gap, Grael named as the receiving authority, and the preliminary concern notice receipt date. Now sealed inside the document roll alongside Silas's chain-record, bound with brass wire and Calvar's wax. One copy. The other
inventory.provenance: Written by Fendt; carried by Silas from the Edge District; now sealed with a second hand into a complete record.

inventory.name: Brass Wire Coil (fine)
inventory.description: A coil of fine brass wire from Fendt's shop — used for sealing sample vessels; precise enough for binding or rune-work.

inventory.name: Chalk Dust Tin (wax-sealed)
inventory.description: Brilliant white chalk dust in a sealed tin — for marking surfaces in poor light or wet conditions.

inventory.name: Pre-Transition Filter Cloth
inventory.description: A tight-woven square of filtering cloth, pre-Transition manufacture — can strain contaminated water through multiple passes.

inventory.name: Pilfered Camp Tin
inventory.description: A small tin from the opportunists' pack — likely taken from someone's unattended camp. Contents unknown.

inventory.name: Trade-Knives (pair)
inventory.description: Two small belt-trade knives confiscated from the road opportunists — plain, serviceable, nothing special.

inventory.name: Seventh-Band Lens-Blanks (tin)
inventory.description: A small wax-sealed tin holding seven unfinished lens-blanks nested in folded linen, plus a slip of paper with grinding measurements in two hands — a margin note reads 'seventh-band, confirm before cutting.' Found abandoned in a dry hollow beneath a neighboring market stall.

inventory.name: Copper Wire Coil (rune-work)
inventory.description: A short coil of fine copper wire — for rune-thread seating and binding work on the road.

inventory.name: Chalk Blanks (pair)
inventory.description: Two pressed chalk blanks for marking and rune-work. Plain, solid, road-ready.

inventory.name: Binding Paste (twist-wrap)
inventory.description: Dried binding paste in a paper twist — for setting rune-work in place. Veth added black salt to the purchase; it holds in wet weather.

inventory.name: Waymarker (father's)
inventory.description: A small disc of pale grey material — neither quite stone nor quite metal — with a single groove worn into its face in a closed oval. His father's thumb wore that groove. Three bonds now seated: the first into Stillwater's Trouble, the second into the Raven's Home warden post, and the third holding the complete four-stage community filtration cascade design — a design, not a place, the first time…
inventory.provenance: Seated into two posts by Silas Weir; now also holding the filtration design as a novel third bond — a use his father likely intended but never wrote down.

inventory.name: Father's Sealed Letter
inventory.description: A folded letter in his father's hand, sealed with a maker's mark — genuine, bone-deep in craft. Written when Silas was four. Kept by Ama until the right moment. That moment is now.

inventory.name: Calling-Slip for Warden Coll
inventory.description: A small folded slip in Ossian's hand — four words, written fast. Gets Silas through Warden Coll's door without an argument.

inventory.name: Letter of Introduction — Warden Coll
inventory.description: A short formal letter in Coll's clear hand — three lines naming Silas Weir's Post Master authority and the Hub Council water committee's standing. Coll's personal seal pressed beside the committee's stamp. Valid for any district-governed contact in the Zone fringe.

inventory.name: Aldric's Water Record
inventory.description: A heavy sheet of paper in Aldric Weir's hand — twenty years of morning water-readings at the Crossing, dated and noted in columns. The final entries are near-daily, and the last line reads: 'It has begun again. He will come.'

deeds.description: Raised a cleaned rabbit from the dead in the upper meadow — no ritual, no preparation, hands and will and the valley's old grain answering
Struck a fair provisioning arrangement with Aldric the smokehouse man — hunting for the village in exchange for food and supplies, and offered to keep watch on what's damaging the river catch.
Silas Weir bound death-runes into the assembled spear at an open-sky fire, with Pell Marsh's maker's mark seated into the blade and Huginn witness at the stone ring.
Coordinated a clean boar kill in the north wood — Corvin landed the strike, Silas held the line and read the ending with a bound spear
Brought down the bull boar on the scrub oak ridge with Pell — a clean hunt despite a misfire in the rune-work.
Delivered a dressed bull and sow to Aldric's smokehouse — a significant haul by village standards, carried down from the north wood by three hunters.
Named the repaired death-bound spear Memory in Pell's forge at dawn — a word that held.
Kissed Pell Marsh at the forge bench at dawn — after a full night repairing Memory together and naming it over old wine.
Persuaded Fendt to commit his testimony to paper and walk to Millbrook — moved the falsified ledger thread from evidence-held to evidence-carried.
Persuaded Calvar — pre-Transition filtration engineer and author of the seventh-band specification — to leave the Edge District and travel to Millbrook to attest against Overseer Grael
Neutralized a relay figure in the cut-lane without violence or alarm — The Ended Threat, Wildcraft, and The Shadow Work braided into a clean exit for Calvar and the document.
Showed mercy to road opportunists after disarming them — named the broad man's grief, gave them provisions, and sent them to honest work rather than leaving them in the mud
Called the key players of the water crisis to Pell's forge for an evening council — Dara, Aldric, Fendt, Mara, and the engineer Calvar, all in one room.
Organized the valley's water-crisis response into four parallel working threads — engineering, logistics, supply, and accounts — with named leads for each, in front of every stakeholder
Sparred Pell at the waygate at first light — belt knife against rune-read blade, came out of it with one real lesson and two feet she said were good
Won a Coliseum bout with a single spoken word — never pressed the weakness, let the opponent decide
Named the road plainly to Veth Ondra — the dead warden post, the Disputed Zone, the valley's water — and offered the compact without embellishment
Seated a ward in the Ent grove circle — a collective working with Pell, Veth, Siol, and Huginn — the grove's own shape as the structure, the Weirmark at the join. The Ent received it.
Named and claimed the Raven's Home warden post as an Ashwarden base — Stillwater's Trouble — planting a working post on the March for the first time in eleven years.
Attended the ending of an old badger in the hollow below the Raven's Home post — sat with it in the plain Ashwarden way, no craft past the clean reading, no ceremony past the presence.
Commissioned Edvar Crane as an agent of Stillwater's Trouble — ending his twenty-year solitary watch and bringing his filtration knowledge into the fellowship's network.
Bound a complete four-stage community filtration cascade — including a detail the shadow found before any of them thought to draw it — into the Waymarker's memory
Closed his father's unfinished fold and made the first new waygate since the Transition — a passage built not by the Numinous, but by the man the lineage was for.
Sealed the made gate with a warded shadow-frame and the Weirmark — the first warded threshold on the March since the Transition

chronicle: The Fell Pell gathering sealed and delegated — Calvar to repair lead, Dara to logistics, Mara to supply and comms, Aldric to accounts, Fendt named to the fellowship, document roll complete and bound for Pip Cotter. Silas and Pell step out into the cold night, the road beginning tomorrow, the forge warm behind them.

The Fell Pell gathering: Pell's brigandine finished with full protective rune-work collar to hem, one radiant mark at the chest from the vial's last scraping, and a partial Shielding Word seated in its outer ring with the promise of completion. Pell's short sword rune-bound with four threads including Huginn's ending-sense and her own ironsense. The forge named the Fell Pell; the fellowship formally opened. Calvar took the repair lead, Dara the logistics, Mara supply and comms, Aldric the accounts; Fendt named to the fellowship and vouched for by Aldric. The document roll sealed with every witness line present, Pip Cotter named as carrier. Silas and Pell settled the road: south lane in the morning, home first, then the Disputed Zone. The coals cooled. The night was quiet.
Silas and Pell sleep, share a last morning meal at the forge, establish a relay protocol with Mara Wells, say their farewells, and step south out of Millbrook at a measured morning hour.
Silas, Pell, and Huginn step through the waygate together at dawn — the road south beginning in earnest.

Silas thanks Tane at the close of the morning bouts, rejoins Siol, and hears her plain assessment of the fight. Siol offers a tour of the Hub — plaza first, Ent circle last — and the scene at the Coliseum reaches its natural end.

The party followed Siol north through the Hub's quieter lanes and arrived at the edge of the Ent grove circle at midday — the path giving way to older ground, the circle of trees ahead, Siol stopping at its edge.

The party stepped through the sixth waygate at the Hub — Siol at the arch's edge, the gate-keeper's instruction plain, the March setting confirmed north-by-northwest. The road to Raven's Home has begun.
(a scene whose summary was lost to a formatting error)

Silas Weir arrived at the Stillwater's Trouble hollow on World-day 19 with Pell, Veth Ondra, and Cassiel Ord — planted Memory at the site's center using three braided crafts with Pell's ironsense as anchor, claimed and named the Raven's Home warden post as his own Ashwarden base, seated two Boundary-Stone wards at the post's crown and the hollow's mouth, led Veth down into the hollow so the eleven-year completion could be witnessed by all four principals, walked the post's interior and named every space — Pell's forge corner, Veth's teaching alcove, Cassiel's keeper's threshold, Huginn's rook, Silas's Maker's hollow — added a shadow-and-boundary ward skin to the walls, invited Veth to demonstrate her March-form threshold-hardening which settled into the base layer, and in the quiet after the work finished, Cassiel named himself keeper of the threshold. The post is claimed, named, anchored, and held.

Silas asked Veth to read the soul bond — she confirmed it plainly, named it rune-in-grain. He announced the road to Cairnhold and the introduction to his mother. The party departed Stillwater's Trouble on World-day 19 afternoon and arrived at Cairnhold's outer district on World-day 23.
The party walks from the western crossing lane to Silas's mother's house in Cairnhold's center district — the road ends at an open door and a chimney smoking.

The party sits with Ama at the kitchen table in Cairnhold — the sealed letter open, the Waymarker seated, the father's work named and understood. Silas promises to return with news from the hollow. Ama folds the letter and gives it back to him for the road.

The evening at Ama's table winds down — Ama shows Veth to the east room, Huginn takes the window ledge, and Silas brings Pell to his quarters. The Waymarker and the father's letter rest on the shelf. The household settles.
Silas and Pell settle into sleep in Cairnhold — the child named, the night complete, morning and its reckoning waiting on the other side of the dark.

Breakfast at Ama's table in Cairnhold — the last meal before the road. Ama names Silas's father's hands. Pell and Veth say their farewells in the register they know best. Silas embraces his mother at the door and steps out with the whole party into the early-spring morning, the Crossing ahead.

The party closes Stillwater's Trouble — three flights of Marrow's Wings, the first Ashwarden attendance, two lessons from Veth, and the hollow known and held — and sets out on the March Road toward the Crossing and Edvar Crane.

The party transits the waygate and arrives at the Crossing — a small road-junction settlement with a mill, a well, boiling-rags on the rail, and the gray-brown tinge of the creek running downstream of the Zone.

Silas Weir met Warden Coll in his registry office and built the full accountability chain — document roll, testimony, signed witness statement with Post Master mark, a shadow-architecture of the failing water system raised from the Waymarker, a permanent two-way shadow-slate bound to the Weirmark seated on Coll's desk, a formal Letter of Introduction sealed with Coll and committee authority, a weekly check-in protocol written into the ledger margin, Maren Ossitide's name given as the one legendary figure the Zone draws near, and Huginn's plain three-sound reading of the crisis: the plans hold weight and will move, but the thing upstream is on its own schedule and the clock has not been seen. The scene closes with the flag near dropping and Silas on the stairs.
Silas thanks Ossian and walks south from the annex back to the waygate marketplace — ZR-OA-7, the suspension order's shape, and the letter all in hand.

Silas offers aid to Renna in exchange for the commission; she declines with even professional courtesy and turns to the work — the boar tusks on her bench, the commission complete, the scene at the stall closed.

Silas delegates lodgings for Crane and Veth to Mara, says goodnight to the assembled group, and walks home through the dark lane with Pell — the night's business done, the departure staged for first light.
Silas seated the Weirmark and spoke the Shielding Word at dawn in Pell's forge — Memory fully complete, the shadow-spear sealed and ready to answer any call from any distance. The work is done.

Silas named his love to Pell plainly at the forge bench at dawn — she received it in her own register and gave it back. Both of them packed for the road without ceremony, and the Fell Pell is ready to be left.
The party steps out of Mara's store at dawn — Pell ready, Veth steady, Huginn aloft — and leaves Millbrook behind for the road south.

chronicle: The party steps south from the waystation at dawn — Pell, Veth, Huginn, and Silas on the road toward the Disputed Zone.

Deep in the left-branch mist, with Cael's steadying grip at his wrist and Pell, Veth, and Huginn attending, Silas Weir brought the wright's close to his father's unfinished fold — the last joint pressed home, the passage made real and repeatable, a gate standing in open ground where none existed. The first made-gate since the Transition, built not by the Numinous, but by the man the lineage was for.

turns.player: Invite the party to each give their own thoughts on the new gate.
turns.summary: The party gives their first readings of the made gate — Pell confirms it holds at every angle with no seam, Veth names the weight of what it means for the March and for the people who will learn of it, Huginn sits on its edge and watches.
turns.narration:
The gate stands in the mist. It is frameless and markless — just an opening in the air where the fold closed, the passage settled into something real and repeatable. The left-branch road stretches away on either side of it, unchanged. You turn to face the others.

Pell is the first to speak. She walks a slow half-circle around the gate's edge, Memory across her back, and her ironsense is plainly working — you can see it in how her weight shifts as she passes through the space. 'It holds,' she says to Silas, not to the gate. 'Solid at every angle. Your father's joint and your close, and there's no seam between them. That's not easy to do, even with the original intention still in the material.' She stops. She does not offer more than that, and she does not need to.

Veth stands where she has been standing since the gate settled — three feet back, still, hands at her sides. She studies it for a long moment before she speaks. 'A made gate,' she says quietly. Not awe exactly. Something more deliberate than awe, closer to reckoning. 'The March has not had a new one in eleven years. The Numinous stopped making them when the Transition came, and no one else has. You should understand what that means in terms of what people will want from you when they find out.' She pauses. 'And they will find out.' She is not warning him against it. She is naming the weight plainly, the way she names every weight plainly, so he can decide how to carry it.

Huginn is on the gatepost — or rather, on the place where a gatepost would be if the gate had one, perched on the air's edge with its wings settled and its eye fixed on the passage. It makes one short sound. Not a word. Not quite not a word. Then it is silent again, looking at the gate the way it looks at things that are ending or beginning, unhurried and entirely certain of what it sees.

*You feel it settle into you — a new steadiness. (Level 25: +1 attunement, +5 reserves, and growth to choose — a sub-attribute point and a skill point.)*

turns.player: Build a proper way gate frame around the  gate using shadow work and the made thing together. Invite the others to add their craft if the would like, add their makers marks if the will it.
turns.summary: Silas attempts to frame the made gate in shadow and wright's craft together, inviting marks — the two threads find nothing to grip and the attempt fails cleanly; the gate stands unchanged.
turns.narration:
You reach for both threads at once — The Shadow Work to give the gate a visible frame, The Raised Thing to make that frame hold. The idea is sound: shadow shaped with a wright's intention, given structure, given permanence. A frame that others could mark. A gate that would look like what it is.

The shadow answers. You pull it into the opening's edge, and for a moment you can feel it taking the shape you want — a threshold, clear-edged, the passage defined on both sides. Then The Raised Thing pushes back. Not against the shadow itself, but against the joining. The two threads reach for each other and find nothing to grip. The Wright's craft wants material. It wants something with weight and grain and history to press against. Shadow does not have any of those things. You hold the attempt for three full breaths, and on the fourth the shadow spills out of the shape you were holding and settles back into the mist at your feet, formless.

The gate stands exactly as it was. Frameless. Markless. Real and repeatable, but nothing added to it — no frame, no invited marks, no visible sign of who made it or who attended.

Pell stops her slow circle and looks at you. She does not say anything yet, but the question is plain on her face. Veth is still, watching the place where the shadow went. Then Huginn, from its perch on the air at the gate's edge, turns one eye toward you and makes a single short sound — not quite a croak, more the noise of something noted and filed. It is not unkind. It is simply precise.

turns.player: Lay out the working model.  A shadow frame, a makers plaque, and a combined warding.
turns.summary: Silas braids The Shadow Work and The Warding Mark into a single craft — a shadow-frame, warded and sealed with the Weirmark, now standing around the made gate on the left-branch road.
turns.narration:
You stop reaching for the frame as a visual thing and start thinking about what a gate actually needs to be. Not a decoration. A threshold. A threshold has a name, a purpose, and a boundary — and those are exactly what The Warding Mark is for.

You pull The Shadow Work up first. The shadow comes easily here, thin spring mist giving it texture to grip. You draw it into the gate's edge — not shaping it decoratively this time, but purposefully, the way you would seat a mark into a post or a lintel. As the shadow settles along the passage's border, you feel what wants to happen next: the shadow isn't just a skin over the opening, it's a field. A field with an inside and an outside. The moment that registers, The Warding Mark moves through the shadow-field like a voice into an open room, and the two lock together.

The gate frame appears. It is not iron and it is not stone — it is shadow that has been told what it is for, and shadow convinced of its own purpose holds a great deal longer than shadow that is merely dark. You can feel the gate's boundary settle into something legible. Not decorative. Structural. Then, without quite deciding to, you press your maker's mark into it — the Weirmark, the same seal that sits in Coll's desk and on Mara's counter. It takes. It sits in the shadow-frame the way a mark sits in wax, crisp and specific.

You open your hand and step back. The shadow-frame stands around the made gate — bounded, warded, sealed with your name. A plaque is not the right word for what is there. A declaration is closer. Veth makes a short sound that is not quite surprise and is entirely recognition. Pell's chin comes up. Huginn does not move, but the quality of its attention shifts — the eye that was watching you is now watching the gate, the way it watches things that have become what they were going to be.

*✦ New technique discovered: **The Declared Threshold** — it's yours now, ready to use.*

turns.player: Invite Veth and Pell to add their own marks to the frame — offer the gate to the people it belongs to
turns.summary: The made gate receives Veth's ashwarden mark — the open-hand of attendance — and Pell's silent ironsense confirmation. The gate now carries the marks of three of the people it belongs to.
turns.narration:
You step back from the warded frame and look at the others.

'It wants more than my mark,' you say to Veth and Pell. 'If this gate belongs to the March, it should carry the March in it.'

Veth studies the shadow-frame for a long moment without speaking. Then she steps forward and touches the edge of it with two fingers, the way you have seen her touch a door she is reading. She does not press through. She holds still, and something in her posture says she is finding the right register for what she is doing. Then, deliberately, she draws a single ashwarden mark into the shadow at the left upright — the warden's open-hand, the gesture that means *attended*. It settles into the frame cleanly, the shadow taking the mark as if it had been waiting for it. She steps back. 'For the ones who come after,' she says to Silas, not to the gate. 'So they know this passage was seen rightly.'

Pell gives the gate one more circuit, Memory across her back. At the right upright, she stops. She does not draw anything. She presses her palm flat against the shadow and holds it there, and the soul bond carries you a flash of what she is feeling — the solid presence of the threshold, the ironsense confirmation of its weight, something that is not quite pride and not quite satisfaction but shares their country. She lifts her hand and looks at you. 'My mark is already in the spear,' she says. 'That's enough.'

Huginn shifts on the gate's edge and says nothing. But it has not moved from that perch since the frame seated, and you have learned by now that the carrion bird stays where things have become what they are supposed to be.

turns.player: Read the gate with Order-Sense — see the full design it is now part of, and what the Zone looks like from where you are standing
turns.summary: Order-Sense reads the made gate as fully part of the March Road design — and shows the Zone ahead as a lattice of old, still-executing threads, all pointing north-and-west toward the watershed where the reclamation site waits.
turns.narration:
You open Order-Sense and let the gate speak.

The made gate sits at the edge of two designs at once. Behind you, the March Road is a clean thing — old intention, well-kept, a structure that knows its own purpose. The waygate network threads through it like a nervous system, and the gate you made is already part of that thread. Not grafted. Part. The March recognizes the passage as a passage, the same way it recognizes Veth's mark at the left upright as an attendance.

Ahead of you, the Zone is different.

It is not hostile. It is not broken. It is — unsettled. The lattice here runs thin and in patches, like ice over moving water, and the designs you can see are old ones that have drifted without anyone to tend them. There are threads running through the Zone that were meant to connect to something upstream, and they do not connect to anything now. They run forward and end in the middle of the air, cut by something that was removed or that stopped working, and the cut ends are still searching. That is the word that comes to you: searching. Not reaching for you specifically. Just still executing an old instruction, patient and unhurried.

The reclamation site is upstream of where you stand. You cannot see it from here, but you can see where the threads point — north-and-west, into the higher ground, where the watershed begins. The searching threads all point the same direction.

Pell says, quietly, 'What does it look like?' She is watching your face, not the gate.

'The March is on one side,' you say. 'And on the other side, there are threads that are still running. Old ones. They are looking for something they were told to connect to, and they have not found it yet.' You pause. 'They all point the same way.'

Veth does not ask which way. She has her own read of this country. She looks north-and-west and says, 'Yes.' Just that.

turns.player: Name the gate's ward aloud — declare what it stands against before you leave it here unattended
turns.summary: Silas names the gate's ward aloud — the declared threshold is complete, its purpose set, and the party turns north-and-west into the Zone.
turns.narration:
You face the gate and speak plainly.

'This threshold stands against what would pass through without knowing what it passes through,' you say. 'Against the careless crossing. Against the one who comes to take without attending.'

The words are not loud. The mist is thin around your boots and the road is quiet. But the shadow-frame hears the declaration the way a lock hears a key — a slight, definite settling. The Weirmark at the seal brightens for a moment, then goes still. The ward has its purpose now. It is not fighting anything. It is simply present, with a name for what it refuses.

Veth exhales once through her nose. 'Good,' she says quietly, and that is all. Pell shifts Memory across her back and looks north-and-west, ready. Huginn lifts from the gate's edge without ceremony, circles once above the threshold, and banks north. He does not look back. The gate stands behind you — framed, warded, declared, attended — and ahead the Zone opens into higher ground and thin mist and the searching threads you cannot see but know are there, pointing toward the watershed.

*✦ What the Water Remembers — Codex: a pre-Transition nanite reclamation system, still running, still following a standing instruction — 'prepare the watershed.' Linked to What Wakes Beneath..*

turns.player: Walk to the gate one more time and set a Boundary-Stone as a second layer — a deterrent beneath the warding declaration
turns.summary: Silas sets a quiet Boundary-Stone as a second layer beneath the gate's warding declaration — the threshold is now double-held, and the party turns toward the Zone.
turns.narration:
You walk back to the gate and crouch at its base.

The shadow-frame is already present and holding — you feel it the way you feel a door closed at your back, that particular quality of weight. You do not need to look at the Weirmark to know it is seated. You have already done that work.

What you are doing now is simpler and smaller. You press two fingers against the ground at the gate's left upright and let Boundary-Stone run quiet — not loud, not urgent, just present. The claim goes into the earth here the way a fence-post goes in: nothing dramatic, just a line the ground knows is there. It is not a challenge. It is an awareness. Something that crosses this threshold without attending will find, beneath the warding declaration, something older and more patient that has already noticed them.

You stand and step back. The gate looks the same. It always will. But it has two layers now — the declaration above, the claim below — and you are satisfied with the proportion of it. Veth watches without comment, which is her version of approval. Pell has her eyes north already, Memory steady across her back, ready to move.

turns.player: Move out — the direction is already named and the threads have told you what they know. Walk into the Zone
turns.summary: The party leaves the made gate behind and walks north-and-west into the Zone — Huginn ahead on a boulder, the ground rising, the mineral smell of the water source already faint on the air.
turns.narration:
You turn your back on the gate and walk north-and-west into the Zone.

The mist is thin at ankle height and the ground underfoot is soft — early-spring mud over old stone, the kind of surface that holds a boot a half-second longer than it should. The road proper ends about forty yards from the gate. Past that it becomes a track, then a suggestion, then just open country rising toward higher ground. The air smells of wet earth and something faintly mineral — the same iron-oxide tang you know from the creek at Millbrook, but quieter here, carried on the cold.

Pell walks at your left shoulder, Memory across her back, eyes on the ground ahead the way a smith reads a casting surface — looking for the flaw before the flaw announces itself. Veth takes the right, her pace even and unhurried, the warden's walk of someone who has crossed this kind of country a great many times. Neither of them speaks. The mist thins as the ground rises and the light, still low and flat, catches the wet grass in long silver lines.

Above you, Huginn drops out of the grey and lands on a lichen-covered boulder forty yards ahead. He sits there facing north-and-west and does not look back. That is the direction. That is what he has read.

turns.summary: Silas takes a quiet scouting flight on Marrow's Wings and spots a warpling hunting along a dry streambed two hundred yards east.
turns.narration:
You stop on the rising track and look up.

The sky ahead is pale and open — flat morning light, no cloud, the mist already burning off the high ground. Room enough to fly, and reason to: Huginn is ahead on his boulder, watching the country, and you would see more from above than from the track.

You bring Marrow's Wings up quietly. The shadow-frame seats across your back the way it always does — not heavy, but present, the death-sense in it giving the air a slightly different weight. You do not push. You lift slowly, a few feet, then more, the ground pulling away beneath your boots as you climb. The wings are dark against the morning sky and they do not make a sound.

Pell watches you go without comment. Veth tilts her head back and reads the sky the way she reads country.

From forty feet up, the Zone opens. The track runs north-and-west as a pale line through old grass and stone. To the east, a dry streambed where something disturbed the silt recently — tracks along the far bank, deep and four-toed, headed toward a stand of dead alder. A warpling. You have seen the pattern before: the stutter-tracks, the way the mud is pressed at uneven intervals. It is moving along the streambed away from you, maybe two hundred yards out, hunting the alder roots. Not close, not aware of you yet.

You hold altitude for a moment, reading the distance and the ground between, then descend back to the track.

turns.player: Move to intercept — close the distance to the warpling along the streambed before it reaches the alder
turns.summary: Silas descends from his flight and cuts the warpling off before it reaches the dead alder — the creature is cornered between the party on the bank and the drop of the streambed.
turns.narration:
You come down from the flight in a long, controlled descent — not rushing, picking your line. The warpling is moving east along the dry streambed, close to the far bank, and from above you can read its pattern clearly: short stuttering bursts, three or four feet at a go, then a pause with its too-many legs bunched under it. It has not scented you yet. The dead alder stand is a hundred yards ahead of it.

You land on the near bank without a sound and move at a low crouching walk along the streambed's edge. The mud is firm enough here — old stone just beneath the surface — and your boots find the quiet line between the loose gravel and the soft patches. The warpling's back is to you. It pauses, legs cycling in that unsettling way, nose working at something in the dry gravel.

By the time it turns, you are thirty feet away and closing. It sees you. The body locks up for a single breath — and then it moves, fast and wrong, angling toward the alders.

You get there first. You angle hard left, cutting the distance at a diagonal, and when it jinks toward the dead trees you are already on the line between it and them. It pulls up short on the bank, all six legs braced, a sound rising from it that is less a noise than a pressure behind the teeth.

Pell arrives at the streambed's far edge a moment later, Memory leveled, reading the ground the way she reads iron. Behind you, Huginn drops from the sky to a dead branch at the alder's edge and sits very still.

turns.summary: The warpling launches from the bank — six-legged, stuttering, fast — and the fight opens on the dry streambed.
turns.narration:
The warpling moves first.

It was a hare once — that much is still visible in the long haunches and the twitching nose — but something in the Zone rewrote the rest. Six legs instead of four, the extra pair set too far back, and the way it moves is wrong: not a run but a stutter, each burst covering ground before your eye has finished registering the last position. It is three feet at the shoulder and it is hungry in a way that has nothing to do with its size.

It comes off the bank at you in a low flat rush, the gravel scattering under all six feet at once.

Pell does not flinch. She calls out from the far bank, clear and short, said Pell: "Left shoulder." Memory is still on her back — she is reading the ground, not committing, holding position as anchor.

Veth's footsteps sound on the track behind you — she is close now, coming up fast, but she is not yet at the bank's edge. You will not have her at your side for the first breath of this.

Huginn lifts from the dead branch without sound. It does not flee. It climbs ten feet and holds there, wings spread, watching the warpling with the particular stillness it reserves for things that are close to ending. It is not an omen. It is simply doing its work.

turns.summary: A warpling cornered on the dry streambed yielded and withdrew — the fight won without a killing blow, the creature still alive and gone east along the bank.
turns.narration:
The warpling stops.

Not slowly — it simply stops, all six legs planted in the gravel, the stuttering rhythm gone still. Its haunches are still bunched. Its nose works the air. But the rush is over, and whatever drove it forward has gone somewhere else.

You are standing on the gravel with Memory in hand, and the warpling is three feet away, watching you with the flat bright eye of a thing that has just decided you are not worth the cost. It holds that still for two full breaths. Then it turns — not fast, not slow — and moves away east along the streambed, each step deliberate, the wrong number of legs carrying it in that stuttering slide until it reaches the shadow of the far bank's overhang and is gone.

Pell exhales through her nose, said Pell: "Good." She does not move from her position on the far bank. Huginn descends from above the alder stand in a long unhurried spiral and lands on a stone three feet to your left. It watches the place where the warpling disappeared. Then it turns its head and looks at you, and says nothing, which from Huginn means the same as saying: that one was not finished yet. Veth comes up over the bank edge behind you, her boots finding the firm stone line without being told where it was. She reads the tracks in the gravel and the stillness of the streambed in one look, said Veth: "It turned. Something in it still works."

quests.title: The Second Thread
quests.premise:
His father left two threads. The first was in a drawer: the Waymarker, and Ama held it until he came asking.

The second could not be left in a drawer, because a drawer holds NOTES and what his father left was WORK — begun, unfinished, and standing somewhere still. He left it with a craftsman named Edvar Crane, at the Crossing, where all roads meet. Fifteen years ago.

The Waymarkers were not surveyors. They were the last people who knew how a waygate is made — and they had never made one. The Numinous built every gate in the world before the Transition, by touching meaning directly, and then dissolved most of the way out of the world that could have taught anyone else. What the Waymarkers held was the leavings: a practice reconstructed backwards from finished gates by people who could not do what the builders did.

Silas's father was trying to finish one. **There is a half-made waygate.** A fold begun and never closed, standing since before the post fell — neither open nor shut, and a fold that is neither is not stable, it is WAITING. It is near the Crossing. Everything crosses at the Crossing.
quests.stakes:
A half-made fold does not stay half-made forever. It resolves, one way or the other, and nobody alive knows which way or when.

And it cannot be finished by a Numinous, because finishing is not what it needs — it was begun by reaching and it has stopped where reaching ends. **It needs a maker's hand to close it and a warden's contact to let it go, and those are the same man exactly once in a generation.** Silas is a wright who tends endings. That is not a coincidence in his lineage. It is what the lineage was FOR.

Whichever he uses shapes what the finished fold IS.

To FINISH: close the fold as a maker closes a joint, and there is a new way through the world where there was none — the first waygate made since the Transition, made by a man who is not Numinous, by a route the builders did not use. To END it: let it go, cleanly, as an Ashwarden lets things go — and the danger stops, the work stops, and his father's unfinished thing is finished by being concluded.

**He can do both because he is both.** That is the whole arc.

Whatever the structure was ordered to do finishes without a single living person having chosen it, and finishing is not the same as stopping.

routes.lattice: Read the array's own instruction set until it's legible enough to touch — not guessed at, known.
routes.ashwarden: Deathsense it directly. It isn't alive the way a person is, but something in it isn't finished being anything else either. Read what an ending means to a thing that doesn't fear its own.
routes.umbral: Go in unseen. Learn what it's actually doing before anyone upstream decides what story to tell about it.
routes.abyssal: Name what the structure wants — to complete its instruction — and treat that want as real enough to bargain with.
routes.stillhold: Broker the standoff first. Get Harmonic and Radiant to stand down long enough to act on the real source together, before either faction owns the answer.

outcomes.name: The Site Sealed
outcomes.summary: The instruction is stopped cold. The water clears. What it was for is buried with it.
narration: The reclamation site goes dark. Within days the Echo River runs clean, and Millbrook's guards stand down from the filtration arrays without a shot fired.

The Archive Guardian does not forgive this easily — a working pre-Transition system, one of perhaps a handful left running in the world, destroyed rather than understood. He is right to be furious and says so.
Whatever the substrate was preparing this watershed for will now happen somewhere else, to someone who didn't get a choice in it either — the Valley's tremor was never the only one.
The district exhales. It does not yet know what it gave up to get that exhale.
Verist disposition toward you: raised — you gave people the plain truth and a clean ending. Lattice: lowered — you didn't need to understand it, only to stop it.

effects.change: sealed — permanently inert, the instruction halted mid-execution

effects.note: a working pre-Transition system destroyed rather than studied; he will not easily trust your judgment on old things again

effects.text: The reclamation site beneath the Disputed Zone has been sealed. What it was preparing the Echo watershed for will never be known here.
Word spreads that the Valley's water crisis had a built source, not a natural one, and that it has been closed for good.
Foreclosure doesn't stop the substrate waking elsewhere — only here. What wakes beneath continues on its own schedule, everywhere the Valley isn't.

outcomes.name: Let It Finish
outcomes.summary: The instruction completes. The water is not restored. It is something else now.
narration: You do nothing to stop it, or you help it along, and the reclamation system runs its last cycle to completion. The poisoning stops — but not because the water went back to what it was.

The Echo River no longer sickens anyone. It also no longer behaves entirely like water. Fish return to it changed in ways no one has words for yet. Nobody drowns in it anymore, and nobody has explained why.

The Archive Guardian is half-vindicated, half-unsettled — this is exactly the kind of thing he wanted preserved and studied, and exactly the kind of thing nobody asked the district's permission to let happen to their river.
You made the opening choice at the smallest scale the largest arc has to offer. What the water became is shaped, now, by what happens to it next — and by who's watching it.
Ashwarden disposition toward you: raised — you let a thing finish being what it was becoming instead of forcing it back into what it had been.

effects.note: fascinated and uneasy in equal measure; wants access to study what the water has become

effects.text: The Echo River is transformed, not restored. Something in the water is different now, and no one fully understands what.
The Echo watershed has changed in ways that reach past the Valley — the substrate's waking is no longer only a tremor here.
What the water has become will need tending, or watching, or both — and it will not wait forever to be decided about.

effects.note: engaging the reclamation site advances What Wakes Beneath on the shared clock — the tremor became a stirring, and everyone sees it

outcomes.name: The Instruction Rewritten
outcomes.summary: Neither stopped nor completed — amended. Someone finally reads it well enough to change it on purpose.
narration: You don't shut the system down and you don't let it run blind. You get inside the instruction itself and change one line: prepare the watershed — for what it can safely become, not for whatever it was originally for.
The water clears. It also carries something new — small, useful, unmistakably still there if you know to look. The district gets its river back and doesn't know it got anything else.
The Archive Guardian is, briefly, insufferable about being right that this was worth understanding rather than destroying or ignoring.
This was the hard way. Reaching it took the technical or death-sensed truth of stages 2 and 3, not just a decision at the end — and it shows in what's left standing.
Lattice disposition toward you: strongly raised — you didn't defeat the thing or surrender to it. You read it well enough to argue with it and won.

quests.title: The Light That Will Not Dim
quests.premise: High Luminary Sera has buried a set of readings, and the reason she buried them is worse than the readings: the Radiant Reach is drifting toward its own extreme faster than the Accords can hold, and the light is winning ground it should share. She wants the truth out before it is forced out — but the truth is that her own people are the ones pulling.
quests.stakes: If you walk away: the buried readings stay buried, the Radiant leadership keeps drifting toward the pole, and the balance the Accords maintain between light and dark loses a Reach's worth of ground — the first Reach to pull free of the middle, and the proof to the others that it can be done. The poles pull harder everywhere once one of them wins.

stages.objective: Learn what Sera's engineer buried.
stages.condition: Obtain the suppressed readings (from Sera, the engineer, or the Radiant archive) OR witness the drift directly at a filtration array.
stages.change: Codex: the Radiant Reach is intensifying past the Accord's tolerance — and someone chose to hide it.

stages.objective: Find who benefits from the light winning.
stages.condition: Identify the faction inside the Radiant leadership pushing the drift (via the readings' chain, a defector, or the Cult of the Unlit's mirror-accusation).
stages.change: Codex: the pull has a party behind it, not just a tendency. The middle has an enemy with a name.

stages.objective: Decide whether the middle is worth holding.
stages.change: The Radiant Reach's drift is checked, accelerated, or turned — and the other Reaches watch which.

routes.verist: Bring the buried readings before the Accord council, plainly, and let the drift be seen for what it is.
routes.stillhold: Broker between the Radiant hardliners and the Accord — hold the middle by keeping both poles in the room.
routes.umbral: Give the Unlit their due — let the dark's counter-claim stand as the balance the light forgot, without letting either win.
routes.radiant: Argue the light back toward its own better nature — a Radiant who refuses the extreme is the strongest answer to the drift.
routes.lattice: Take the readings apart until the drift is undeniable arithmetic, not a matter of whose word to trust.
routes.abyssal: Name what the drifting faction actually fears — the dark, the middle, being ordinary — and offer them a way to stop pulling that isn't surrender.

outcomes.name: The Middle Held
outcomes.summary: The drift is checked; the Accord holds; the light shares its ground again.
narration: Sera's readings land where they had to, and the Radiant leadership — some of it furious, some of it relieved — steps back from the pole.
The Accord holds. The other Reaches, who were watching to see whether a pole could be made to stop pulling, see that it can.
Sera is spent and vindicated and not entirely grateful to have been made honest. She will remember which you made her.
Stillhold disposition toward you: strongly raised — you kept the room together when it wanted to split.

effects.note: made honest against her own people; owes you and resents the debt a little

effects.text: The Radiant Reach's drift toward the pole was checked; the Accord held. The first proof that a pulling pole can be made to stop.

effects.note: holding the middle keeps the arc from advancing — the pull is checked here, though it continues elsewhere

effects.text: Word spreads that a Reach was pulled back from its own extreme — the Accords gain a precedent, and the pulling factions everywhere gain a warning.

outcomes.name: Let the Light Win
outcomes.summary: The drift completes; the Radiant Reach pulls free of the middle.
narration: You do not stop it, or you help it — and the Radiant Reach pulls hard enough to break the Accord's hold on it. The light wins its ground.
It is not a disaster you can point at. It is brighter now, and cleaner, and less willing to share the world with the dark — and the other Reaches have just learned that a pole can win.
Sera got her truth out and lost the thing the truth was supposed to protect. She does not thank you.
This is the arc's fork answered toward the pole: the middle lost a Reach, and the pull got stronger everywhere.

effects.note: her truth freed the drift instead of checking it; she holds you partly responsible

effects.text: The Radiant Reach pulled free of the Accord's middle. The first pole to win — and proof to the others that winning is possible.

effects.note: a pole winning advances The Poles Pull — the drift becomes strain, everywhere

effects.text: The Radiant Reach has broken toward its pole; across the Reaches, the pulling factions take heart and pull harder.
One pole winning teaches the others. The next Reach to pull will not bury its readings — it will point at the Radiants and say it was allowed.

dara-holt-the-ditch-mother.voiceHints: Broad-shouldered, mid-fifties, hands that look like they were carved from the same hardwood as a shovel handle. Speaks in measurements and seasons — 'that valve's been weeping since last thaw,' not 'something's wrong.' Never dramatizes. Brings a cracked fitting to prove the point before she finishes the sentence. Calls a problem by its part name, not by its consequence.
knowledge: Forty years of the eastern channels — every slope, silting pattern, and freeze-line in the network

The river's mineral load has shifted since late autumn: fittings that lasted a decade are threading out or snapping in under two seasons, and the corrosion pattern runs inward from the joint, not outward the way sediment wear does
Three other irrigators on the eastern bench are seeing the same losses but haven't connected them yet — she has
The stretch of river above Holt's intake smells faintly wrong in still mornings, a faint bitterness she can't name but recognizes as new
She keeps a tin of failed fittings sorted by failure date and location — a physical record no one asked her to keep
dara-holt-the-ditch-mother.wants: Replacement valve stock she can trust, a forge-backed answer for why her iron is failing, and confirmation that the river is the cause — not her installation work. She is not here to be reassured; she is here for a diagnosis.
dara-holt-the-ditch-mother.fears: That the river is doing something the valley has never budgeted for and that this spring's planting window will close before anyone in authority admits it.

kit.reveal: Brings physical evidence — dated, sorted, labeled — that makes the river's pattern undeniable to anyone willing to look at the parts
kit.bind: Connects isolated reports from neighboring irrigators into a coherent problem, naming the network's shared vulnerability before it fragments into blame

reactsToReputation.dismissive-or-theoretical: polite, brief, and gone — she'll find someone who works with their hands
reactsToReputation.curious-and-honest: stays longer than she planned, starts drawing channel maps on whatever surface is available

bette-harrow-the-seed-ledger.name: Bette Harrow, the Seed Ledger
bette-harrow-the-seed-ledger.role: Contract seed-agent for the upvalley growers' cooperative, collecting outstanding grain-debts before the expedition locks up the forge accounts
bette-harrow-the-seed-ledger.voiceHints: Mid-forties, weathered apron, ink-stained fingers. Speaks in numbered points without meaning to — 'First. Second. Done.' Knock was three times, flat and evenly spaced, the knock of someone who has knocked on a hundred doors this season and will knock on a hundred more. Carries a wax-sealed ledger book under one arm and smells faintly of thaw-mud and linseed. Does not waste warmth, but is not cold — simply occupied.
knowledge: Pell's forge owes the cooperative fourteen measures of worked iron against last autumn's seed-credit — the debt was rolled once already and the cooperative cannot roll it again before spring planting
Three other valley craftsmen settled accounts this week; Pell is the last open line
She heard at the mill this morning that the forge party is departing today — that is exactly why she knocked before seventh bell
The cooperative's eastern field irrigation channel needs a new sluice plate; she is authorized to negotiate that ironwork as partial settlement if Pell is short on coin
She knows Corvin Aldric by name and reputation and was relieved it was neither of them who answered — she finds them harder to settle with than a working smith
bette-harrow-the-seed-ledger.wants: Close the account today, in full or in trade, before the expedition leaves and the debt floats until midsummer. She has fourteen other stops before noon and the mud on the south lane is already soft.
bette-harrow-the-seed-ledger.fears: That the forge will be shuttered for weeks mid-season and the cooperative will have to explain to the upvalley families why planting is delayed because of an uncollected iron-debt — her name is on that ledger too.

reactsToReputation.honest-dealer: softens immediately, willing to negotiate trade-in-kind with a handshake and no witness
reactsToReputation.debt-dodger: produces the ledger, reads the clause aloud, does not raise her voice, does not leave

She can produce the binding obligation in writing on the spot (bind), and if a party disputes a figure she can walk the arithmetic aloud, line by line, until the error or the truth surfaces (reveal). No magic. Just ink, memory, and early-spring light through a forge doorway.

pip-cotter-mara-s-errand-runner.name: Pip Cotter, Mara's Errand-Runner
pip-cotter-mara-s-errand-runner.role: Child courier and small-task helper for Mara Wells
pip-cotter-mara-s-errand-runner.appearance: Seven years old, possibly eight — she is unsure and will tell you both ages depending on which she remembers. Wears an oversized blue wool coat that was someone else's first, the cuffs rolled four times and still dragging. Cheeks red from the cold and the running. Clutches whatever she's carrying in both hands like it is the most important object in the world, because Mara said so.
pip-cotter-mara-s-errand-runner.voiceHints: Breathless sentences, pauses to swallow air mid-thought. Repeats Mara's instructions almost verbatim before adding her own opinions uninvited. Calls adults by full name because that is what she has heard done. Takes promises seriously and remembers them exactly.

kit.move: Knows every shortcut between Millbrook's lanes and garden gates — the gap in the Cotter fence, the stepping-stones behind the mill, the path along the east ditch that stays dry into spring.
kit.reveal: Absorbs overheard details without meaning to and repeats them with complete accuracy when she trusts the listener, or when she forgets to be careful.

knowledge: The contents of the cloth Mara sent — she memorized Mara's words about it before she left, in case the cloth got wet
Every house in Millbrook that keeps a dog and which ones bite
That Mara has been up before dawn three mornings running — Pip noticed because she was also up, feeding the goat
Which neighbor children are sick this season and which are not — valley gossip absorbed from doorstep conversations while waiting to be let in
pip-cotter-mara-s-errand-runner.wants: To complete the errand correctly, catch her breath, and be given a small task on the return trip so the journey feels useful twice.
pip-cotter-mara-s-errand-runner.fears: Losing or ruining something she was trusted to carry. Being told she arrived too late.

reactsToReputation.trusted-by-mara: opens up immediately, will answer two questions for every one asked
reactsToReputation.unkind-to-children: goes quiet, delivers the message in the fewest possible words, leaves fast

pip-cotter-mara-s-errand-runner.notes: Not yet aware that she is a reliable source of low-level local intelligence. Mara is aware. Pip is loyal to Mara first and will report any strange treatment back to her without being asked.

provenance.hint: a girl of seven or eight in an oversized blue wool coat — Mara's errand-runner, practical and out of breath

Pip reached the halfway waypoint ahead of schedule and, while waiting for the gate-keeper to log her passage, talked her way into carrying a sealed reply-note back — the return trip now has its small purpose, and she is quietly pleased with herself.

Pip delivered the package to the right door and, on the way back, was handed a folded note by the recipient's housekeeper to carry to a tailor two streets over — the return trip now has its own small purpose.

calvar.name: Calvar
calvar.role: Pre-Transition filtration engineer, author of the seventh-band monitoring specification — a man who stopped moving fifteen years ago because the light in one room told him everything he still needed to know
calvar.physicalDetail: Late fifties, though early-spring morning light makes him look older — the kind of age that comes from stillness, not hardship. Hands still precise. Keeps the window above the cooperage angled so the first plateau light crosses his drafting surface at exactly the seventh-band frequency. He has calibrated this by hand, yearly, for fifteen years.
calvar.voiceHints: Unhurried in a way that is not rudeness — he simply will not be rushed past the part that matters. Speaks about light the way other engineers speak about load-bearing calculations: not reverently, but exactly. When he senses evasion he goes very quiet and waits, and the waiting is harder than argument. Will not leave a sentence technically imprecise even when it costs him emotionally.

abilities.reveal: Calvar reads spectral signatures in ambient light the way others read handwriting — he can identify filtration drift, contamination band, or a falsified purity reading from the quality of illumination in a room. This is not mysticism; it is fifteen years of sitting still with the seventh band until it became a language.
abilities.bind: The seventh-band specification is a living instrument to him. He knows every node it touches, every engineer who trained under it, every deviation that has ever been logged. Persuading him is not a social act — it is a technical one. Give him a true reading and he is bound to it. Give him a false one and you have lost him entirely.

knowledge: The seventh-band monitoring specification in its entirety, including three unpublished addenda he chose not to file
What the diagram he left with Leth three days ago means — and what it does not mean, which is the more important half
That the seventh-band readings have been drifting in a direction that has no name in the pre-Transition literature, and has had no name for eleven months

The cooperage below him has been storing something other than barrels for two seasons; he has not reported it because the light it emits is not dangerous — it is, in a way he cannot yet specify, attentive
That leaving the room means losing the calibration, and that losing the calibration means the specification becomes a document rather than a living thing
calvar.wants: To be given a reason to leave that is technically sound — not an appeal to safety, not an appeal to duty, but a reading he cannot take from this window. He will go if the data requires it. He will not go for sentiment.
calvar.fears: That the drift in the seventh band is not contamination but communication, and that moving before he understands it will mean the message arrives and no one is left who can read it.

reactsToReputation.truthful: he opens the second notebook, the one he has not shown anyone
reactsToReputation.technically_credible: he treats you as a colleague and the conversation shifts from persuasion to collaboration
reactsToReputation.evasive_or_political: he answers every question accurately and volunteers nothing; the diagram becomes the whole of what you get

calvar.relationshipToLeth: Trusts Leth's judgment about people, not about urgency. The diagram was a gift, not an alarm — he expected Leth to sit with it for a month, not three days.
calvar.currentState: Early spring has shifted the morning angle two degrees north. He has been recalibrating since first light. The seventh-band reading this morning was the clearest it has been in eleven months, and he is not certain whether this means the drift is resolving or peaking.

Calvar ran a manual recalibration of the seventh-band sensor overnight and found a three-point drift he cannot yet attribute to instrument error or source change — he has written nothing down, but he has not looked away from the window.

Calvar noticed a drift of 0.003 in the seventh-band baseline reading and spent the night re-checking his instruments rather than the sky, unwilling to admit whether he is hoping to find instrument error or confirm the drift is real.

A subtle drift appeared in the seventh-band readings overnight — within tolerance, technically, but not within the pattern Calvar has memorized across fifteen years, and he has been sitting with that deviation since before dawn, deciding whether it is the window finally failing him or finally telling him something new.

Calvar recorded a seventh-band reading at the same hour he always does, but this time he wrote a small asterisk beside the value and did not immediately explain it in his log — the first annotation without an accompanying sentence in eleven years.
The window gave him nothing that technically required him to move — the data stayed ambiguous, and so did he.

A gap opened in the cloud cover at an hour when it shouldn't have, and the readings it produced don't match the model he has been trusting — not wrong enough to act on yet, but wrong enough that he wrote the discrepancy down, which is the first crack in his reason to stay.

A gap in the cloud cover last night gave Calvar an unusually clean read, and the numbers came out slightly wrong — not wrong enough to be certain, but wrong enough that he wrote the figure down twice and underlined it.

vash.name: Vash
vash.role: Piecework lens-grinder of the Edge District — the one whose wheel was turning before the district woke, and who understands the array's optical layer the way water understands a crack
vash.voiceHints: Unhurried. Speaks in the cadence of someone who has spent years listening to the pitch of a wheel and knows that rushing ruins the curve. Does not perform ignorance but does not announce knowledge either — waits to see whether you are asking the real question or the surface one. When she decides you mean it, she will tell you exactly what she heard, what she saw, and what she made of it, in that order, without decoration.
knowledge: The fresher notation on the diagram — she heard Calvar speak it aloud, half to himself, while waiting for Leth's door; she did not know what it meant then and has been turning it over since
The optical layer of the array at a depth the weavers who commission her work do not suspect: she grinds to tolerances they specify without understanding why, and she has come to understand why
Which lenses in the eastern relay cluster were reground on non-standard prescription, and whose chit authorized it — she kept the chit because the prescription was wrong in an interesting way
That Leth's archive door carries sound badly, and that the east room is the worst-kept secret on the row
vash.wants: To understand what she overheard well enough to know whether she should have said something sooner. She is not afraid of consequence — she is afraid of having held a piece of something important and not known what it was a piece of.
vash.fears: Being made into a witness for something she only half-understood. That the half she missed is the half that matters.
vash.physicalDetail: Fine-grained abrasive dust has settled permanently into the creases of her hands and the inner corners of her eyes. In early-spring light, standing near a window, she looks briefly like she is made of the same material she works.
vash.dailyPattern: At the wheel before first light. Done by mid-morning. Afternoons she is difficult to find — she walks the valley rim, which the district assumes is idleness and which is not.

Vash spent the evening re-grinding a lens she'd already finished, turning the fragment of overheard conversation over in her mind until she placed it — the word used wasn't a maintenance term, it was a calibration term, and that distinction has been quietly unsettling her ever since.

Vash spent the quiet hours between grinds tracing back what she overheard against the small things she knows about the array's optical layer — a particular phrase she'd dismissed as jargon now sits wrong in her, not quite matching the geometry it should describe, and she has not yet decided whether that wrongness is hers or theirs.

Vash spent part of the night re-grinding a lens she had declared finished, the repetitive motion giving her cover to turn the overheard fragment over and over until she isolated the one word in it she still cannot place — and now she is nearly certain it was a name, not a process term.

Vash placed the overheard phrase against something she already knew and felt the two pieces click together — she still doesn't have the whole shape, but she now knows the piece she held was real, and that it mattered.

She turned the overheard words over again today but reached no new edge — the piece still doesn't show her what it belongs to, and she is no closer to knowing whether her silence was an error or simply a pause.

dav-cutter.name: Dav Cutter
dav-cutter.role: Cut-cord relay watcher for Grael's network — posted to the south cut-lane behind the cooperage barrel-yard, reading arrivals and passing word
dav-cutter.voiceHints: Young enough that his stillness costs him something — he practices it. Speaks rarely and in pieces: a half-sentence, a direction of the chin, a breath held too long. Valley-grain runs through him despite himself; he reads the quality of silence the way a lay-brother reads scripture, and he knows when a light has changed before he can say how. Hand never leaves the left lapel of his coat. When Silas came through the gate, Dav felt it like a shifted candle-flame — and has not yet decided what the feeling means.
knowledge: The relay hand-signs Grael's cutcords use along the south cooperage lane — three variations for stranger, known, and known-and-wrong
The rhythm of the barrel-yard: which hours the coopers go quiet, where the gate shadow falls in early-spring morning light
That Silas came through — the shape of his arrival, not yet its meaning
The Low Lamp's back-passage geography well enough to be gone before a question becomes a confrontation
That the valley's stillness is not emptiness — it is attention, and he has learned, uneasily, to trust that
dav-cutter.wants: To pass the word clean and be done — no interpretation, no consequence, just the relay completed and the coin earned. He is quietly afraid that this particular message will not let him stay that simple.
dav-cutter.fears: That the valley's light will eventually make him legible — that something in the stillness here will read him back the way he reads arrivals, and that what it finds will cost him the cord.

abilities.description: Passes encoded hand-signal up the network without voice or paper — stranger, known, or known-and-wrong. The message moves; he stays. The valley stillness carries it faster than it should.

abilities.description: Dav can vacate a lane so cleanly that witnesses reconstruct him out of ambient detail — a barrel stave, a shadow, the smell of new wood. In the valley's strong light, this costs him more than it used to. The light keeps finding edges.

A plaza vendor who had grown used to Siol's quiet presence reported them to a Hub registrar as a loiterer without a declared purpose, and now there is a notice requiring Siol to either state their business in writing or move on by the following morning.

A hub official stopped Siol at the plaza's inner gate to check travel papers — the papers are in order, but the stop itself drew looks, and the brief public scrutiny is exactly the kind of attention Siol's quiet passage depends on not receiving.

maren-voss.name: Maren Voss
maren-voss.role: Liminal fighter who crosses thresholds to win — patient at every gate, lethal the moment one opens
maren-voss.voiceHints: Speaks the way someone waits — fully, without fidgeting. Grey coat, collar up against the early-spring cold she doesn't seem to feel. Answers questions a beat after you expect, not because she's slow but because she's already past your question and choosing which part of the answer is worth giving. Never names her companions first; lets them step through on their own terms.
knowledge: The Waygate's threshold-logic — which passages open early, which resist, and what the valley asks before it lets you through
How to read a bout before it starts: the other fighter's weight on their threshold moment, when they commit, the half-step that gives everything away
That the Coliseum far arc rewards those who make their opponent cross into unfavourable ground — and she has walked every arc of it in her mind

companions.name: Aldric

companions.note: Older, steady, doesn't smile much; has been at this long enough that his calm is the real kind

companions.role: Second second — young enough to be nervous, sharp enough to be useful; scouts ground and brings her water without being asked
companions.note: Talks when Aldric doesn't, which means the two of them together cover everything

abilities.name: Threshold Step
abilities.description: Maren reads the liminal beat of any exchange — the half-moment a gate swings — and steps through it before her opponent has committed. She does not dodge; she is simply no longer where the blow was aimed, and she is already at the next threshold.

abilities.name: Gate Hold
abilities.description: She can stall a passage — freeze the moment of transition for herself or a companion — holding a threshold open or shut long enough to change the shape of a fight. Used defensively, it is a ward; used offensively, it pins an opponent mid-step.

abilities.name: Far Arc Patience
abilities.description: In the Coliseum's far arc, where sight lines are long and the crowd loses track, Maren goes still enough to become part of the threshold itself — then crosses the distance in a single passage-movement that reads as arrival, not approach.

maren-voss.wants: One clean bout at the far arc, properly offered. She has been at the Waygate since the first thaw, waiting for her name to come up through the right mouth. She does not want shortcuts; she wants the gate to open the right way.
maren-voss.fears: That she will be read as ordinary before the bout begins — that whoever faces her will arrive with a fixed idea of what a grey-coat threshold-walker does, and she will have to spend the whole fight correcting it instead of fighting.

tane-solr.name: Tane Solr
tane-solr.role: Threshold-walker and named bout opponent — a man who has crossed the center-line enough times to stop counting and started watching the sand instead
tane-solr.voiceHints: Unhurried in a way that is not laziness but arithmetic — he has already run the numbers on you and does not need to rush. Speaks in short declaratives with long pauses between them, as if he is giving the words time to land before he adds more weight. Calls the sand 'the floor' the way carpenters call wood 'the material.' Does not brag. Does not diminish. Names things exactly. When he says your name he means it.
tane-solr.appearance: Lean in the way the valley's early-spring wind is lean — nothing wasted, everything purposeful. Grey coat, collarless, worn to the colour of old flint at the cuffs. Two seconds coiled at his left hip, their grip-wraps re-done so many times the cord beneath has fused into something that is no longer rope and not yet bone. Dawn finds him standing at the far arc before the torches are lit, not warming up, just watching the center-line as if it owes him a conversation.
knowledge: The Waygate Coliseum's far arc — every degree of angle the pre-dawn light hits the sand, and what it does to a fighter's depth perception
How the valley's threshold law reads a bout: where the line is, what crossing it costs, and the three ways experienced fighters use the cost as a weapon
The particular grammar of two seconds — reach, wrap, redirect, the half-breath of slack that telegraphs everything if you know to listen for it
Silas's name, and therefore something about Silas — enough to have agreed to the bout, not enough to have made up his mind
tane-solr.wants: A bout that is true — not won or lost but honest, where both fighters come to the center-line having brought everything they actually are and no more.
tane-solr.fears: That he has crossed so many thresholds he no longer feels them, and that the day he stops feeling the line underfoot is the day he becomes dangerous for the wrong reasons.
tane-solr.history: Tane came up through the valley circuit in a leaner season, when the Coliseum ran bouts by firelight because they could not afford dawn slots. He lost his first twelve named matches and won the thirteenth by not moving when every instinct in the crowd — and his opponent — was certain he would. He has been studying stillness as a weapon ever since. The grey coat was his instructor's; she died between seasons, not on the sand, and he has not replaced it. He is not sentimental about this. He is precise about it.

cassiel-ord.name: Cassiel Ord
cassiel-ord.role: Former march-warden who walked away from the post and sat down in the bowl and has not decided what comes next
cassiel-ord.voiceHints: Economy of words born from years of writing terse post-reports nobody acted on. Does not explain himself unless pushed, and when pushed gives one careful sentence more than expected and then stops. The silence after he speaks is not unfriendly — it is the silence of someone who has learned that most follow-up questions answer themselves if you wait. Stillwater grain: surface calm, something held under it that has not been named yet.
knowledge: The March in the years bracketing Veth's posting — patrol routes, seasonal flood-lines, which threshold markers are still true and which have drifted
Why the Veth post was dissolved, or at least the version of it he was given, and the part of it he does not believe
The Raven's Home threshold: he has crossed it twice, knows what it costs, knows what it gives back, and will not say more than that without trust he has not granted yet
Early-spring snowmelt read from limestone and sky — when a valley like this will sheet-flood and how much warning you actually get
The name of whoever ordered the dissolution and what that person's interests are in the March going unwatched
cassiel-ord.wants: To sit here long enough to know whether what he is feeling is conscience or exhaustion — and to answer that honestly before he moves again.
cassiel-ord.fears: That the dissolution was not incompetence but intent, and that knowing it changes what he is obligated to do with the rest of his life.

reactsToReputation.warden_or_posted: goes very still, then asks one quiet question about where and when before he decides anything

cassiel-ord.appearance: A lean man somewhere in his middle forties, the kind of lean that is not hunger but habit — he has been moving through difficult ground for a long time and his body organized itself around that. March-warden coat, wool, the grey-green of limestone shadow, one brass closure replaced with knotted cord. Boots still muddy from the threshold. He is sitting with his back to the outcrop and his knees drawn up, not sleeping — just not moving. His face is weather-seamed and unhurried, the expression of someone who has decided to be still until he is ready not to be. There is a short-handled field axe laid flat beside him, not gripped, not put away.
